newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota plans output on extra days in Oct.
newsitem.headline: Toyota plans output on extra days in Oct.

text.p: Some Toyota Motor Corp plants will operate for extra days in October to boost production of new models, a Toyota spokesman said on Wednesday.
The Tsutsumi plant's No. 2 line, the Tahara plant's No. 1 line, and the Kyushu plant will each operate for two extra days in October to boost output.

Toyota had 8,500 domestic orders for its Windom model in the first month after its launch, compared with a monthly target of 3,000. The new Land Cruiser Prado, HiLux Surf, and Mark II were also seeing strong domestic demand, the spokesman said.
Toyota received a total 33,000 domestic orders for the Mark II and its sister Chaser and Cresta models in the first 11 days after their launch, far above a monthly target of 23,500.
Toyota Auto Body Co Ltd, which is owned 44.1 percent by Toyota, will operate for three extra days in October to boost output of Toyota's new Estima, Estima Lucida, Estima Emina and Ipsum.
Hino Motors Ltd, which is owned 11 percent by Toyota and another affiliated company, will also operate for one extra day in October to produce Toyota cars, he added.
